title: DataArchitectureItems
description: Shape of content.items for L1-design-data-architect. The artifact (data-architecture.md) is the authoritative, human-readable document; items restates the same facts in queryable structured form so downstream consumers (L1-design-integration-architect, L1-design-platform-architect, L1-arch-baseline-generator, L1-testing-env-provisioner, L1-testing-synthetic-data-generator, gr-L1-architecture-conformance) can read ownership, classification and conformance without parsing markdown. Meta-points pattern: every narrative field here is a capped summary; the full prose lives only in the artifact. Two invariants are enforced structurally rather than left to prose. First, one writer per entity — entity_ownership names exactly one owning_context per entity and the entity values are unique, so a second writer is not expressible. Second, no invented governance value — a retention or residency of PENDING must carry a pending_ref into pending_decisions, and a non-PENDING value must carry a source, so a plausible-sounding period with nothing behind it fails validation rather than shipping into a register that reads as decided.

entity_ownership.description: DAT-1.1, one entry per entity in the FSA's APP-3 aggregate model — same names, same order, none added, none dropped. This is the system-of-record register PRIN-02-C1 evaluates.

classification_register.description: DAT-3.2, covering the same entity set as entity_ownership in the same order. PRIN-06-C1 checks classification AND retention AND residency together, so all three are required fields — 'PENDING' is a permitted value, silence is not.

events.description: DAT-2.2 initial event register. May be empty only where the FSA's component map contains no asynchronous edge at all — which is unusual enough that the reasoning should say so.

data_planes.description: DAT-4. The operational plane entry is always present. An analytical plane entry is present even when the decision is NOT_PRESENT — recording the deferral and its trigger is the decision, and omitting the row turns a deliberate deferral into a silence nobody can reopen.

read_models.description: DAT-6 replication register. Commonly empty at Cycle 0 — an empty array is the correct expression of 'None at Cycle 0' and is not a gap.

demand_traceability.description: DAT-7. One entry per REQ-DAT-* demand, per CON-* constraint whose binding viewpoints include DAT, and per principle applied. A demand with no entry is an unanswered demand, which must instead appear in open_questions.

conformance_checks.description: DAT-9. At minimum the three the viewpoint always owes: one writer per entity, no unregistered replication, and protected data has classification+retention+residency. Written as expressions a checker evaluates, never as prose.

pending_decisions.description: DAT-8. Every deferred decision, each with the trigger that reopens it. A pending decision without a trigger is a silence, so trigger is required.

open_questions.description: Gaps this agent could not close and must not paper over — an FSA entity two contexts both appear to need to write, a regulatory posture that does not answer a retention question, a REQ-DAT demand with no satisfying decision.

entity.description: The entity name exactly as the FSA's APP-3 model states it — never renamed, never pluralised differently, never invented. Unique across this array: a repeated entity is a second writer expressed as two rows.

owning_context.description: Exactly one bounded context from the FSA's APP-1, and it must exist there. Ownership is assigned to a business capability — never to a team, a service name or a database (PRIN-02).

system_of_record.description: The authoritative store for this entity, named at capability level (e.g. 'Catalogue persistence'), not as a physical table or instance.

classification.description: From kb-L1-enterprise-security ES2. Must equal the classification for the same entity in classification_register — the two tables disagreeing is exactly the drift DAT-3's register exists to prevent.

source.description: Where the ownership assignment came from: the FSA section that names the entity, or the KB rule that settled a contested assignment.

confidence.description: 0.9+ where the FSA states the owner outright; 0.7-0.8 where it was inferred from which context's invariant the entity protects; below 0.7 should be paired with an open_questions entry.

reasoning.description: Why THIS context owns the entity — which invariant it protects, or which heuristic decided a contested case. Not a restatement of the entity's purpose.

ClassificationEntry.description: One DAT-3.2 row. PRIN-06-C1 fails on a missing residency exactly as it fails on a missing retention, so all three are required — the permitted way to say 'not yet decided' is the literal 'PENDING' plus a pending_ref, never an absent field and never a plausible value.

entity.description: Matches an entity in entity_ownership exactly.

retention.description: The retention rule, or the literal 'PENDING'. A value here is either stated by the PRD's regulatory posture, by kb-L1-enterprise-security ES3, or by a REQ-DAT demand. '6 years is typical for financial records' is an invention with a citation-shaped wrapper and must be PENDING instead.

residency.description: The residency rule as an approved operating region per ES9 — never a concrete cloud region id, which is a platform decision — or the literal 'PENDING'. Never silently defaulted to the platform's home region.

source.description: Required whenever retention and residency are both non-PENDING: the standard or requirement that grounds them.

pending_ref.description: Required whenever retention or residency is 'PENDING' — the DAT-8 row carrying the trigger that reopens the decision. A PENDING with no trigger is a silence.

encryption_required.description: True for every PII, Financial, Confidential and Regulated Evidence entity per ES10. The data viewpoint states the requirement; the platform viewpoint selects the realisation.

event_type.description: Canonical {context}.{entity}.{event} naming, lowercase, dot-separated. The context segment is a bounded context name — never a team, system or product.

owner_context.description: The producing context, which owns the event's business meaning. A consumer never becomes owner of the entity behind it.

purpose_summary.description: Capped summary — what this event tells downstream. Full description lives in the artifact.

version_state.description: 'Planned' means the architecture recognises the contract but the producing feature has not necessarily been implemented. At Cycle 0 nearly everything is Planned; an 'Active' event before any feature exists is a defect.

version.description: Semantic version of the event contract, once one is assigned.

plane.description: Which DAT-4 plane this entry decides.

decision.description: 'NOT_PRESENT' is a real, defensible Cycle 0 decision — a platform is not created because it may eventually be useful — but it obliges a trigger.

realization_summary.description: Capped summary of the technology and ownership model. This document MAY name a technology; the FSA may not. Required when decision is REQUIRED.

trigger.description: Required when decision is PENDING or NOT_PRESENT: the condition that reopens the decision, stated as a condition and not a date.

pending_ref.description: The DAT-8 row for a PENDING plane decision.

lifecycle_check.description: PRIN-07-C1 outcome for a named technology: that its lifecycle status is not contain/retire, or the exception that permits it. Required whenever realization_summary names a product.

ReadModel.description: A registered replication. PRIN-02-C2 checks that every attribute mirrored from another context has one of these; an unregistered copy is a second writer in slow motion.

source_owner.description: The bounded context that owns the source entity — the read model does not transfer ownership.

staleness_budget.description: How stale the consumer may tolerate. A read model without a declared staleness budget is uncontrolled replication with a nicer name.

demand_id.description: The FSA demand, the cross-viewpoint constraint, or the principle — id exactly as the source states it, never renumbered.

satisfied_by.description: The DAT section that answers it. A demand answered nowhere belongs in open_questions instead of being given a hopeful row here.

satisfaction_summary.description: Capped summary of HOW it is satisfied — the decision, not a restatement of the demand.

check.description: A machine-evaluable expression over the design artifacts — e.g. 'for every critical entity: count(authoritative_writers) == 1'. Prose here makes the check unevaluable, which makes it a slogan.

decision_summary.description: Capped summary of what is not yet decided.

trigger.description: The condition that reopens this decision. Required with no exception — PRIN-01-C1 checks exactly this, and a pending decision with a date instead of a condition just expires quietly.

question.description: The decision someone has to make, phrased so it can be answered — not a restatement that something is unclear.

origin.description: 'ownership_ambiguity' is the one to watch: two contexts both appearing to need write access to an entity is a boundary problem in APP-1, raised against the FSA — never resolved here by permitting two writers.

doc_location.description: The DAT section where this question is visible in the artifact. A question recorded only in items is invisible to everyone who reads the document.
